1. Study Title: The Brain STEM program: Transforming STEM training using neural and artificial intelligence modeling.

2. Study Procedures: The goal of this research is to better understand learning of skills critical to STEM careers (spatial reasoning and computational thinking) and how learning of these skills inform our general understanding of neural plasticity in the brain. This study will take approximately 30 minutes; participants will be asked to do one computerized task where you will see some brief stimuli (for example, objects), and make judgments about them.


3. Participant Inclusion: Individuals between the ages of 18 and 65 with normal or correct-to-normal vision and normal color vision.


4. Participant Exclusion: Individuals with impaired vision should not participate in the present study.


5. Risks: There are no known risks associated with participating in this experiment.


6. Investigators: The following investigators are available for questions about this study
Dr. Melissa Beck mbeck@lsu.edu
Stephanie Saltzmann ssaltz2@lsu.edu
Dr. Alex Cohen acohen@lsu.edu
Dr. Greening sgreening@lsu.edu


7. Right to Refuse: Subjects may choose not to participate or to withdraw from the study at any time without penalty or loss of any benefit to which they might otherwise be entitled.


8. Privacy: Results of this study may be published, but no names or identifying information will be included in the publication. Participant identity will remain confidential unless disclosure is required by law. All data collected will be stored on a password protected computer and no names will be associated with the data being stored on said computer.


9. This study has been approved by the LSU IRB. For questions concerning participant rights, please contact the IRB Chair, Alex Cohen, 578-8692, or irb@lsu.edu.


10. By continuing this experiment, you are giving consent to participate in this study.


11. Your information or biospecimens collected as part of the research, even if identifiers are removed, may be used or distributed for future research.
